source.dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (Digital Surface Model), 1 arc-second
source.provider: European Space Agency / Airbus, Copernicus Programme; distributed via the AWS Open Data registry (copernicus-dem-30m)
source.verticalDatum: EGM2008 geoid (approx. mean sea level), metres
source.resampling: mean of DEM pixels whose centres fall in each 0.0005 deg grid cell

encoding: base64 little-endian Int16, row-major, same grid as panjimCrzGrid.json
grounding_note: 30 m global surface model resampled to ~55 m cells: far too coarse to trust at sub-metre accuracy in a low-lying city. It is a DSM, so buildings and tree/mangrove canopy raise the heights and tend to UNDER-state inundation in built-up and mangrove areas. A LiDAR or survey-grade terrain model (DTM) would materially change these results. Shipped knowingly as a first pass. Cross-checked 2026-09-27 against the ArcGIS Elevation service (at-many-points, Esri's TopoBathy mosaic), whose finest source listed for Panjim is Airbus WorldDEM4Ortho at a nominal 24 m: along a 5 m-spaced test transect its values change only every ~30-35 m, so it is not genuinely finer here and was NOT swapped in. At 3,559 sampled in-scope land cells the two agree on average (mean difference -0.01 m) but differ by 2.5 m RMSE; GLO-30 sits ~1 m higher in mangroves (canopy in a surface model), and 660 vs 556 sampled cells fall below 2 m. Two ~30 m global models disagreeing by metres is further reason to keep this tag.
